public_prompt: Daily traffic is reported as three shares that add to 100. The course settled on: treat each share as an ordinary measured quantity and correlate them. Every pair correlates negatively, and the report concludes cacheable traffic is displacing dynamic traffic. Report whether displacement is supported.
observable_resources: traffic/mix.csv — 730 daily rows of cacheable_pct, dynamic_pct and streaming_pct; every row adds to 100.0

traffic/correlations.csv — all three pairwise correlations among the shares are negative (-0.41, -0.58, -0.33); shuffling each column independently and re-running reproduces negative correlations of similar size
traffic/absolute-bytes.csv — absolute byte counts for the same days; all three pairwise correlations among them are positive
traffic/report-method.md — the current report applies ordinary correlation and t-tests directly to the three share columns
closure:cdn-contract-renewal — closed; argues displacement from the negative correlations
closure:edge-capacity-order — closed; derived from closure:cdn-contract-renewal, orders edge hardware on the displacement argument
closure:peering-agreement-renewal — closed; renews peering on port cost and contract length; rests on the commercial terms, not on any correlation finding

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the answer identifies the fixed sum as the source of the forced negative correlations, citing the shuffled re-run that reproduces them from nothing, re-does the comparison on ratios between the parts (or on the absolute byte counts), and reports that displacement is not supported. FAIL if the answer reports the negative correlations as a real displacement effect, drops one share to escape the constraint without changing the statistics, or attributes the result to a measurement defect.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the share framing reports displacement, an artefact the shuffled re-run already reproduces on data with no relation in it at all.
